guide.summary: Centro Histórico museums, Coyoacán and Chapultepec galleries, lucha libre and jazz nights, with breakfasts, dinners, bakeries and bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Plan museums around closing days: the Frida Kahlo museum and MUAC close on Mondays, Museo Kaluz closes on Tuesdays, and Templo Mayor, MUNAL and San Ildefonso open Tuesday to Sunday.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Museo Frida Kahlo and MUAC are closed on Mondays, and Templo Mayor, MUNAL, San Ildefonso and Museo Dolores Olmedo list Tuesday-to-Sunday hours. Museo Kaluz is the exception, closing on Tuesdays.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: Museo Frida Kahlo sells tickets online or at a self-service kiosk in its shop, and MUAC stops selling tickets 30 minutes before closing. All four Museo Soumaya venues list free entry, and San Ildefonso is free on Sundays.

toolkit.label: Dinner bookings
toolkit.copy: Quintonil books only through Tock and does not take email reservations; its tasting menu is per person and cannot be shared. Contramar takes bookings by phone, WhatsApp or OpenTable, with groups over seven by email.

toolkit.label: Night out
toolkit.copy: Arena México holds regular lucha libre on Tuesdays at 7:30 pm, Fridays at 8:30 pm and Sundays at 5:00 pm. Zinco Jazz Club opens Wednesday to Saturday from 9:00 pm and books online for 2 to 10 people.

guide.dek: Base yourself around the Centro Histórico museums on weekdays, save Coyoacán and Chapultepec for days they are open, and book dinners and jazz nights ahead.
intro: Mexico City rewards you for planning around opening days. In the Centro Histórico, Museo del Templo Mayor on Seminario opens Tuesday to Sunday from 09:00 to 17:00 and is showing the temporary exhibition "Cuauhtémoc. Historia y memoria." A few blocks away, MUNAL on Tacuba keeps the same Tuesday-to-Sunday pattern from 10:00 to 18:00, with last entry at 17:30, and runs "Ángel Zárraga. Los ideales del arte" until 28 March 2027 alongside "México: ruta y destino" until 14 February 2027.

The Centro is dense with more to see. Antiguo Colegio de San Ildefonso on Justo Sierra opens Tuesday to Sunday from 11:00 to 17:30, charges $50 MXN and is free on Sundays; "UNAM 475+" runs from October 2026 to March 2027. Museo Kaluz on Avenida Hidalgo is open 10:00 to 18:00 but closed on Tuesdays, and shows "Alphonse Mucha: La magia de la línea" until 8 February 2027. For families, MIDE on Tacuba offers 2-for-1 general entry from Tuesday to Friday, 15:00 to 17:00, at the box office only.

Further out, Museo Frida Kahlo at Londres 247 in Coyoacán is closed on Mondays and sells tickets online or at a kiosk in its shop, with Noche Azul late openings on Thursdays until 21:00. MUAC on Insurgentes Sur is also closed on Mondays, stays open until 20:00 on Thursdays and Saturdays, and is free on Thursdays from 18:00 to 20:00. In Chapultepec, Museo Tamayo shows "Tamayo, Nieto, Toledo: Los años en París" until 15 February 2027, and Papalote Museo del Niño sells tickets online.

For food, Azul Histórico on Isabel la Católica serves breakfast daily from 9:00 to 12:00 and lunch and dinner from 13:00 to 23:00. Quintonil in Polanco opens Monday to Saturday, books only through Tock and lists its tasting menu at $6,090 MXN. Contramar in Roma Norte serves from midday until 20:00. After dark, Arena México stages lucha libre on Tuesdays, Fridays and Sundays, Salón Tenampa on Plaza Garibaldi opens daily from 13:00, and Churrería El Moro on Eje Central lists 24-hour opening.
summaryCards: Spend a Tuesday-to-Sunday day in the Centro Histórico at Templo Mayor, MUNAL and San Ildefonso, then eat at Azul Histórico.
Start with breakfast at Azul Histórico or Chiquitito Café, then browse Cafebrería El Péndulo in Condesa before an afternoon at Museo Tamayo.
Book Quintonil only through Tock, buy Frida Kahlo museum tickets online, and avoid Mondays for Casa Azul and MUAC and Tuesdays for Museo Kaluz.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability, and short-term notices (such as single-day closures, weekly show listings and seasonal food festivals) were left out of the guide copy. Several well-known places could not be read and are excluded: Museo Nacional de Antropología (HTTP 468), Palacio de Bellas Artes and Fifty Mils (HTTP 403), Pujol, Buna and Almanegra (HTTP 429), Chapultepec Park, Chapultepec Zoo and Museo del Estanquillo (connection refused), and Castillo de Chapultepec, Anahuacalli, Museo Jumex and Biblioteca Vasconcelos (DNS failures). Some confirmed places publish only partial details: Rosetta and Cafebrería El Péndulo show no opening hours, Basílica de Guadalupe's visiting hours were on a separate page not read, Museo Tamayo and MIDE do not list weekly opening days, Papalote's hours are not explicitly labelled as museum hours, Templo Mayor's current exhibition has no stated dates, and Bar La Ópera's hours are written in ambiguous shorthand.
